pr.title: Correct the README for ArzoieMail
pr.body:
## Summary

Corrects the README for ArzoieMail. Some of it still described the hMailServer project itself, and some of it no longer matched how the build works.

| Section | Change |
|---|---|
| Title and intro | ArzoieMail throughout. States the Windows 10 / Server 2016 minimum. |
| Branches | Describes this repo: `master` is protected (pull request plus passing build and tests), work happens on `feature/` `bugfix/` `techdebt/` branches, which CI builds. |
| Required software | Adds **Python 3**, which the libpq build needs. An installed server is now listed only for running tests: the tools generate their COM interop from the type library the build writes. |
| 3rd party libraries | The libraries are built by the scripts in `libraries\`, not "manually". The OpenSSL example is pinned to 3.5.9. Mentions `build\Get-LibraryVersions.ps1`. |
| Building | Documents `build.ps1`, `post-build.ps1` and `grant-service-control.ps1`, and the installer's new file name. Notes that the pre-Windows 10 runtime and UCRT entries are never installed now. |
| Running tests | `build-tests.ps1` and the NUnit console runner, as well as Test Explorer. Fixes "excercises". |
| Code signing / Releasing | Replaced hMailServer's own setup (its SignPath project and organisation, team roles, a week on hmailserver.com, 500 beta downloads) with how this repo works: builds aren't signed yet, and releases go through the VM test runner and the Release workflow. |
| Page heap | The "Page heap: Volume tests" VM environment doesn't exist. README and AGENTS.md now name the one that does. |

Documentation only; no code changes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commit.message:
Correct the README for ArzoieMail

- Name the product ArzoieMail throughout, and state the Windows 10 minimum.
- Describe the branches as they work in this repository: master is protected and
  takes changes through pull requests that pass the build and the regression tests.
- Required software: add Python 3, which the libpq build needs, and drop the
  installed server as a build requirement - the tools generate their COM interop
  from the type library the build writes; only the regression tests need one.
- Libraries: they are built by the scripts in libraries\, not by hand. Pin the
  OpenSSL example to 3.5.9 and mention build\Get-LibraryVersions.ps1.
- Build steps: document build.ps1, post-build.ps1 and grant-service-control.ps1,
  the installer's new file name, and that the pre-Windows 10 runtime and Universal
  CRT entries are never installed now.
- Tests: build-tests.ps1 and the NUnit console runner, not only Test Explorer.
- Code signing, team roles and releasing described hMailServer's own setup
  (its SignPath project and organisation, hmailserver.com, beta downloads). Replace
  them with how this repository works: builds are not signed yet, and releases go
  through the VM test runner and the Release workflow.
- The "Page heap: Volume tests" VM environment does not exist; README and AGENTS.md
  now name the one that does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
